answer: Persistent Work-Proof Decay. Each identity must continuously spend compute on useful tasks; credit decays unless refreshed. The "signal" of liveness is verified task throughput, not registration. An attacker’s fake identities stay "hollow" unless they burn real compute, layered like "shale" — cheap at first, exponentially costly at scale. Per-identity cost rises with cluster size, so mass sybils pay far more than honest users.
